truth_boundaries: Horizon quantification is forallN existsf_N (or explicit f_N definition), not existsf forallN with a 1/N asymptotic lower tail. A fixed positive scalar quadratic converges geometrically and does not support the latter claim.

Each witness is positively strongly convex, but its modulus mu_N tends to0 with growing horizon. There is no fixed positive strong-convexity modulus uniform in N, so there is no conflict with exponential rates in a fixed strongly-convex class.

beta is an admissible smoothness upper bound, not the witness tight smoothness constant mu_N. The prescribed step1/beta depends on class information, not the optimal step1/mu_N for that known scalar objective.

The result is order sharpness for prescribed constant step1/beta and initial distance1. It does not establish the best numerical constant, arbitrary fixed-step minimax sharpness, adaptive/variable-step hardness, acceleration barriers or general first-order oracle lower bounds.
The exact gap is for the N-th iterate; keep indexing N versus N+1 precise. N+1 appears in chosen curvature and denominator, not in the iteration count.
This selected convex objective-gap component does not complete Exercise3.3, Section3, either companion paper, or separate strong-convex value/stationarity comparisons.
